## PyQt5-WinARM64 5.15.11.post1: fixed release

**This release replaces 5.15.11, which is broken. Please upgrade.**

```powershell
python -m pip install --upgrade PyQt5-WinARM64
```

### What was wrong with 5.15.11

The 5.15.11 `PyQt5-WinARM64` wheel was published **without the Qt runtime**. It
contained the PyQt5 bindings, but not `Qt5Core.dll`, `Qt5Gui.dll`,
`Qt5Widgets.dll` or the `qwindows` platform plugin. Importing PyQt5 fails with
`DLL load failed` on any machine that does not happen to have a native ARM64
Qt 5.15 on `PATH`.

The wheels attached to the 5.15.11 GitHub release also had a malformed
`.dist-info` directory, which makes pip crash with `InvalidVersion: 'info'`
when it reads its installed packages. The copies on PyPI were not affected by
this second problem.

If you installed 5.15.11 from the GitHub release assets and pip now fails with
`InvalidVersion: 'info'`, remove the broken metadata folders from your
environment's `Lib\site-packages` (`pyqt5_winarm64-info.dist-info` and
`pyqt5_sip_winarm64-info.dist-info`) and the `PyQt5` folder, then install again.

### What is in this release

| Wheel | For |
| --- | --- |
| `pyqt5_winarm64-5.15.11.post1-cp39-abi3-win_arm64.whl` | CPython 3.9+ on Windows ARM64 |
| `pyqt5_sip_winarm64-12.17.0-cp313-cp313-win_arm64.whl` | CPython 3.13 |
| `pyqt5_sip_winarm64-12.17.0-cp314-cp314-win_arm64.whl` | CPython 3.14 (new) |

- PyQt5 5.15.11 built against Qt 5.15.19 (qtbase), natively for ARM64
- Qt runtime, `qwindows` platform plugin and other Qt plugins bundled in `PyQt5\Qt5`
- ARM64 MSVC C++ runtime (`msvcp140.dll` and related DLLs) bundled, so the
  Visual C++ Redistributable does not need to be installed
- PyQt5-sip 12.17.0 for CPython 3.13 and 3.14

### How this was verified

Every wheel is checked for a valid `.dist-info`, a matching `RECORD`, the
presence of the Qt runtime and ARM64 PE headers on every `.pyd` and `.dll`.
The wheels are then installed by name on a **fresh** Windows ARM64 runner with
no Qt anywhere on the machine, on both CPython 3.13 and 3.14. The smoke test
fails unless `Qt5Core.dll`, `Qt5Gui.dll` and `Qt5Widgets.dll` are loaded from
the installed wheel and the Qt plugin path points into it.
